# package transport

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/transport"
```

Package transport is the DNP3 transport function (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 8): it splits application fragments into segments that fit one link frame and reassembles received segments into fragments.

Each segment is one transport header octet (FIN, FIR and a six-bit sequence number) followed by up to MaxSegmentData octets of the fragment. The package keeps the sequence state of one direction of one association; it does no I/O.

## Constants

```go
const (
	// MaxSegmentData is the largest part of a fragment one segment
	// carries: a link frame's 250 octets of user data minus the header.
	MaxSegmentData = 249

	// MaxSegment is the largest segment, header included.
	MaxSegment = MaxSegmentData + 1

	// DefaultMaxFragment is the default limit on reassembled fragments,
	// the size most outstations and masters use.
	DefaultMaxFragment = 2048
)
```

## Variables

```go
var (
	// ErrEmpty reports a segment without a header octet.
	ErrEmpty = errors.New("transport: empty segment")

	// ErrNoFirst reports a segment without FIR while no fragment was
	// being assembled.
	ErrNoFirst = errors.New("transport: segment without FIR outside a fragment")

	// ErrSequence reports a segment whose sequence number does not follow
	// the previous one; the partial fragment is discarded with it.
	ErrSequence = errors.New("transport: unexpected sequence number")

	// ErrTooLarge reports a fragment that grew beyond the limit; it is
	// discarded.
	ErrTooLarge = errors.New("transport: fragment too large")
)
```

Reassembly errors returned by [Reassembler.Add](#func-reassembler-add). Each reports a segment, and possibly the partial fragment before it, that was discarded; the Reassembler stays usable.

### type Reassembler

```go
type Reassembler struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Reassembler rebuilds fragments for one direction of an association.

#### func NewReassembler

```go
func NewReassembler(max int) *Reassembler
```

NewReassembler returns a Reassembler that accepts fragments of up to max octets. A max below 1 selects DefaultMaxFragment.

#### func (Reassembler) Add

```go
func (r *Reassembler) Add(segment []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

Add processes one received segment. It returns the fragment when the segment completed one; the fragment is a new slice owned by the caller.

The rules are those of IEEE 1815-2012 clause 8.2.1.2: a FIR segment always starts a new fragment, discarding any partial one; a segment without FIR must carry the next sequence number of the fragment in progress, or it and the partial fragment are discarded.

#### func (Reassembler) Pending

```go
func (r *Reassembler) Pending() bool
```

Pending reports whether a fragment is partially assembled.

#### func (Reassembler) Reset

```go
func (r *Reassembler) Reset()
```

Reset discards a partial fragment, for example when the link is reset.

### type Segmenter

```go
type Segmenter struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Segmenter splits fragments for one direction of an association. The zero value starts with sequence number 0.

#### func (Segmenter) Segment

```go
func (s *Segmenter) Segment(fragment []byte) [][]byte
```

Segment splits fragment into segments, each ready to be the user data of one link frame, and advances the sequence number. A fragment of zero length is sent as one segment with only the header.

#### func (Segmenter) Seq

```go
func (s *Segmenter) Seq() uint8
```

Seq returns the sequence number of the next segment.
